It is further the case of the petitioner that petitioner and prosecutrix developed good friendly relations.
Friendly loans were exchanged inter se the petitioner and prosecutrix.

the .
husband of the prosecutrix came to know about inter se relations between the petitioner and prosecutrix.
The petitioner was given beatings by the husband of the prosecutrix and accomplices regarding which, FIR No.17 of 2023 has been registered.

3. Per contra, the prayer of the petitioner has been opposed by the learned Additional Advocate General on the ground that there are serious allegations against the petitioner, which are under investigation.
In case, the petitioner is ordered to be released on bail, he may tamper with the prosecution evidence and may try to win over the prosecution witnesses.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have also gone through the entire record carefully.

5. Status report filed on behalf of the respondent/State reveals that in her complaint dated 29 th January, 2023, the prosecutrix has alleged of being sexually exploited by the petitioner on 1st April,
2021 and July, 2021.
It is alleged by her that the petitioner had forced her to enter into relationship with him under the threat of blackmailing her.

She further alleged that the petitioner had taken loan of Rs.1,20,000/- and had returned only Rs.80,000/-.
6.
Thus, from the averments made in the petition and also the status report filed on behalf of the respondent/State, it is clear that the petitioner and prosecutrix have levelled counter allegations.
However, one thing admitted by both is the existence of friendly relations between them.
Nothing has been brought on record to suggest the nature of material available with the petitioner to blackmail the prosecutrix.

The prosecutrix is a .
married woman and a Government servant.
She had sufficient maturity and hence, the reasons for not reporting the alleged unwarranted advances of petitioner towards her for such a long period remains unexplainable.

7. Though, this Court at the time of deciding the bail application will not minutely scan the material collected by the investigating agency yet the same is being looked into only for the purposes of assessing the gravity of allegations against the petitioner.
8. The petitioner is permanent resident of village Challara, P.O. Sinhuta, Tehsil Sinhuta, District Chamba, Himachal Pradesh.
There is no expression of apprehension that he will not be available to face the investigation and trial, if so, required.
Nothing is to be recovered from the petitioner.

sentences.text: Pre-trial incarceration cannot be ordered as a matter of rule.
No ground for custodial interrogation of petitioner has been made out.
In such circumstances, no fruitful purpose shall be served by allowing the petitioner to be kept in custody.

10. The apprehension of respondent/State that the petitioner may tamper with the prosecution evidence, in the event of his release on bail, can be taken care by putting the petitioner to appropriate terms and conditions.

The petitioner was admitted to interim bail on 1st February,
2023.
It is not alleged against him that the petitioner has not joined the investigation thereafter.

11. Keeping in view the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the instant petition is allowed and in the event of arrest of petitioner in case FIR No.17/2023 dated 29.1.2023, registered .
under Sections 376 (2) (D), 323, 506 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, at Police Station, Chowari, District Chamba, H.P, he shall be released on bail subject to his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of Arresting/Investigating Officer.

This order shall, however, be subject to following conditions:-
(i) That the petitioner shall make himself available for investigation as and when required.

(ii) That the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to nay police officer;
(iii) That the petitioner shall not leave the country without the prior permission of the Court.
12. However, it is made clear that the observations made hereinabove shall have no bearings on the merit of the case and shall be construed for the disposal of the present petition only.
(Satyen Vaidya) Vacation Judge 17th February, 2023 (CS)
